title: FlashAttention v2/v3 compatibility sweep and prefill latency calibrator
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Background: Over the last two quarters we've onboarded multiple FlashAttention kernel variants (v2 and v3 derivatives) across different hardware profiles. We've observed intermittent prefill spikes and subtle quality regressions when heuristic kernel selection picks newer v3 paths under certain sequence-length and quantization combinations. This ticket scopes a systematic compatibility sweep plus a runtime "latency calibrator" that can detect regressions early and adjust kernel selection thresholds automatically.
goal: Build a repeatable compatibility sweep across v2 and v3 kernels and add a prefill latency calibrator that (1) produces per-model, per-arch threshold recommendations for selecting v2 vs v3 paths, (2) surfaces regressions in CI/canary, and (3) drives a guarded rollout policy (automatic soft-fallback when SLOs deviate).
success_metrics: Reduce prefill P95 latency regression occurrences attributed to kernel selection by >= 80% vs baseline
CI canary alerts for kernel-induced latency regressions within 30m of rollout
Automatic calibrator recommendations accepted or applied for >= 90% of models in the test catalog without manual tuning
scope_in: Microbench harness for v2/v3 kernels across seq-len buckets, quantization profiles (fp16/int8/q4), memory/tiling configs; runtime calibrator service; canary integration and dashboarding for prefill latency; guarded rollout policy that can hot-swap kernel choices or fall back to v2 paths.
scope_out: Changes to model architecture or training; global runtime refactor outside kernel selection interface; GPU driver or kernel rewrite beyond configuration knobs.
approach: 1) Design a microbenchmark corpus representing realistic prefill distributions (chat startup – short prompts, long-context retrieval – long prompts, and mixed). 2) Run automated sweeps across v2/v3 kernels and quantization profiles on target arches (A100-80GB, H100, and Ampere-40). 3) Capture detailed traces: token startup, KV allocations, workspace usage, per-kernel time breakdown, memory pressure. 4) Implement a lightweight calibrator that consumes microbench results and produces per-model scoring rules: a small rule set with confidence and fallback thresholds. 5) Integrate calibrator into canary rollout (server-side flag) and add an alert when observed prefill P90/P95 exceeds calibrated threshold by > 20%.
experiment_plan: - Phase 1: Synthetic sweep (local infra) across 10 representative models and 3 seq-len buckets to generate baseline matrix. - Phase 2: Extended run across 50 models on H100/A100 hardware to find edge cases. - Phase 3: Canary rollout for small customer segment using calibrator-derived rules. - Phase 4: Full rollout with continuous calibration and periodic re-training of rules.
data_collection: Collect microbench outputs as CSV/Parquet uploaded to S3: columns include model, arch, kernel_variant, seq_len, batch_size, quant_profile, workspace_bytes, token_latency_ms (startup and steady), gpu_util, mem_alloc_error, perf_counters. Use existing perf dashboards and add a calibrator view for threshold recommendations.
rollout_plan: 1) Off-line sweep and recommendation generation. 2) Deploy calibrator as a config-service feature flag. 3) Enable on canary fleet (5% of traffic) for 48 hours. 4) If no alerts and regression count < 1 per 24h, expand to 25% then 100%. 5) If calibrator flags regressions, auto-fallback to v2 path for affected model+arch and open rollback PR for manual review.
risks: Calibrator overfits to synthetic workloads and misses real production distributions
Canary fleet insufficiently representative -> false negatives
Automatic fallback may hide correctness bugs in v3 that should be fixed instead of bypassed
Increased CI runtime due to expansive sweeps could slow developer flow
mitigations: Include real sampled production prefixes (anonymized) in microbench corpus when R&D allowed
Start with conservative thresholds and require two consecutive CI canary failures before automatic fallback
Tag all auto-fallbacks in audit logs and require a follow-up bug for permanent fixes
Limit nightly sweep to targeted model subsets and keep long-run nightly job separate so PRs are not blocked
acceptance_criteria: Microbench harness runs end-to-end for chosen model set and produces a recommendation matrix
Calibrator service exposes recommendation API and can be toggled via runtime feature flag
Canary integration emits alerts when observed prefill P90/P95 deviates from recommendation by threshold
Observed reduction in kernel-selection regression incidents on canary fleet compared to baseline within 72 hours
tasks: T1: Define microbench corpus and create runner (Mateo)
T2: Implement kernel sweep harness, collect perf artifacts (Ivy)
